records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — The credential-sync fetch has no timeout or abort signal, allowing a stalled endpoint to hang every dependent calendar or conferencing operation indefinitely.
records.rationale: Verifiable from the diff: the new fetch in refreshOAuthTokens.ts posts to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT with only method and body — no AbortSignal/timeout — and this function now wraps token refresh for google, hubspot, lark, office365, zoom, webex, zoho. A stalled sync endpoint would indeed hang those operations. This is a substantive, specific, diff-grounded operational/robustness concern rather than a correctness defect, since the code behaves correctly when the endpoint responds.

records.issue_text: packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:88 — The shared endpoint is documented to return only access token and expiry, but Webex rejects it unless it also reproduces Webex's scope, token type, and refresh-token response schema.
records.rationale: refreshOAuthTokens.ts comments 'The response should only contain the access token and expiry date', and the Webex adapter passes its result directly to handleWebexResponse without the parseRefreshTokenResponse/minimumTokenResponseSchema shim used in the Zoom adapter to fabricate a missing refresh_token. So when credential sharing is enabled, the Webex refresh path plausibly fails on missing fields (token_type, scope, refresh_token). The mechanism is grounded in the diff; exact downstream expectations of handleWebexResponse aren't fully visible, so confidence is moderate.
